root_cause.text: On UP (SMP=n) systems, `spin_lock(&pcp->lock)` is used in functions like `drain_pages_zone()` without disabling interrupts, allowing an interrupt context to re-enter the same lock via `spin_trylock()` (which always succeeds on UP) and corrupt the per-CPU page (pcp) structure.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message state: "in drain_page_zone() we are in a section protected by spin_lock(&pcp->lock) and then get an interrupt that attempts spin_trylock() on the same lock. ... the SMP=n spinlock implementation assumes spin_trylock() will always succeed, and thus it's normally a no-op. ... it could cause a corruption of the pcp structure." The patch introduces `pcp_spin_lock_maybe_irqsave` which replaces `spin_lock` with `spin_lock_irqsave` on !SMP && !PREEMPT_RT to prevent the nesting.

The patch introduces `pcp_spin_lock_maybe_irqsave` which replaces `spin_lock` with `spin_lock_irqsave` on !SMP && !PREEMPT_RT to prevent the nesting.

candidates.rationale: Takes the per-CPU pages lock without disabling interrupts; on UP systems, an interrupt handler can re-enter this lock via spin_trylock (always succeeds), leading to corruption of the pcp structure.
This operation modifies the pcp structure while holding the lock. If an interrupt re-enters and performs the same bulk free, the list and count fields become corrupted.
Acquires the pcp lock without disabling interrupts; on UP, this allows interrupt context to re-enter the lock and corrupt shared data.
Executed under the unprotected lock; concurrent interrupt re-entry can cause double frees or list corruption.
Locks pcp without interrupt masking; on UP, an interrupt can grab the same lock via spin_trylock, leading to nested modification of the pcp data.
Modifies the per-CPU page list while holding a non-interrupt-safe lock; re-entrancy from an interrupt can corrupt the linked list and count.
Acquires the pcp lock without disabling interrupts; on UP, this makes it possible for an interrupt handler to concurrently modify pcp flags, causing inconsistency.
Writes to pcp flags under a lock that is not interrupt-safe; if an interrupt re-enters and also writes to flags, the final value may be a mix of intended changes.
